question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[X{Y}^{2}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}1,\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=x{y}^{2}.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ nonzero only in the rectangular region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1\}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X{Y}^{2}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}x{y}^{2}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}x{y}^{2}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}x{y}^{2}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[\frac{{y}^{3}}{6}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
